summary: 1948 metal live-in cab on a tower replacing a 1920s lookout on Elliott Knob; now fenced and closed, reached on foot only.

access.note: Tower is fenced with barbed wire and described as closed; the jeep trail is closed to public vehicles, so access is on foot only.

visit.trail_note: Reached on foot; several trails and the closed jeep trail lead up the mountain.

corrections.why: The register's and SummitPost's 30-foot tower is about 9.1 m. The 3.7 m figure matches the 12-foot steel house on top, so the record may have captured the house rather than the tower. A Forest Lookouts page quoting a 1957 survey gives about 45 feet, which is disputed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and SummitPost give a 30-foot tower (about 9.1 m); a Forest Lookouts page quoting a 1957 survey gives about 45 feet. The 30-foot figure is used because two sources agree; the 45-foot figure is marked disputed.

The register says the lookout can be reached by road or trail, while Wikipedia says the jeep trail is closed to public vehicles and public access is on foot. Both hold: motor vehicles are kept out and walkers reach the summit.

notes_for_editor: No source read gives staffing history, fire history, or the date the lookout closed; the story says only that it is described as closed. The register's height figure prints as '30 tower' with no unit, so the 30-foot reading rests on the register plus SummitPost. The 2018 Staunton News Leader history article (newsleader.com) returned HTTP 403 and may hold staffing history. The brief's elevation (1347.5 m) was not checked. Wikipedia search snippets give the summit as 4,463 ft (1,360 m), which should be checked against a page read before use.
